title: Paul Bourdareau Launay — Cybersecurity & development
desc: Portfolio of Paul Bourdareau Launay, second-year Computer Science Bachelor's student at Ynov, focused on cybersecurity: network hardening, application security, databases.
lead: I build applications and networks starting from one question: who is allowed to do what? Allowlist firewalls, least privilege in the database, authentication verified on the server.
about.1: Second-year Computer Science Bachelor's student at Ynov Campus Paris Ouest, after a French technology baccalauréat (STI2D ITEC). I code in Go, Python and TypeScript, and I'm heading toward cybersecurity.
about.2: What interests me: understanding how a system falls so I can close it better. Writing a firewall from a flow matrix, stripping a SQL account of everything it doesn't need, rejecting a token whose signature hasn't been verified.
about.3: Away from the terminal: 3D design, photography, sports, video games.

defense.sub: Each layer, a measure I actually put in place, and the project that proves it.
l1.p: nftables allowlist firewall (policy drop), WAN / LAN / DMZ zones, stateful tracking, DNAT, logging of rejected packets.
l2.p: Key-only SSH, passwords disabled, root login forbidden.
l3.p: Passwords hashed with bcrypt, constant-time comparison, signed and expiring JWTs, OAuth tokens verified by Ed25519 signature (JWKS).
l4.p: Server-side validation (Pydantic, Zod), parameterized queries, no sensitive value accepted from the client.
l5.p: Row Level Security, NOLOGIN business roles, column-level GRANT, per-profile views: least privilege.
l6.p: Secrets kept out of the repo, CORS restricted to known origins, strict CSP and security headers.
files.sub: Five projects where security is in the code, not in the description.
c1.p: Three-zone Linux gateway (WAN, LAN, DMZ) protecting an internal server and a web intranet. Second-year networking lab.
c1.2: Rules derived from a flow matrix, one row = one rule
c1.3: conntrack state tracking, invalid packets dropped, ping limited to 5/s
c1.4: DNAT to publish the web server in the DMZ, masquerade on the way out
c1.5: SSH: key only, no root login
c2.p: Crypto trading simulator with virtual money, real prices and a player leaderboard. React, FastAPI, PostgreSQL.
c2.1: bcrypt, constant-time comparison, no hint about whether an email exists
c2.2: Expiring HS256 JWT, verified on every private route
c2.3: Google / GitHub sign-in: Ed25519 signature verified via JWKS, plus issuer, audience and expiry
c2.4: The price is never accepted from the client; transactions use row locks
c2.5: Restricted CORS, parameterized queries, secrets kept out of the repo
c3.p: Chase game between friends with real-time positions on a map. Next.js 15, Supabase, MapLibre.
c3.1: Postgres Row Level Security: the browser only holds the anon key
c3.2: Role-filtered view: a hunter can't read what the hunted sees
c3.3: Every input validated on the server with Zod
c3.4: RLS tested in SQL with 6 simulated accounts, including one outside the game
c4.p: PostgreSQL database for a manga lending library, 200,005 loans. Second-year advanced SQL group project.
c4.1: NOLOGIN business roles, one account per person inheriting from them
c4.2: UPDATE granted on a single column, readers' emails unreadable at the front desk
c4.3: Per-profile views: the manager reads statistics, nothing else
c4.4: Trigger that enforces the business rule inside the database itself
c4.5: Index on a foreign key: query about 40 times faster
c5.p: REST API for a game catalog. FastAPI, SQLAlchemy, Pydantic, PostgreSQL.
c5.1: securite.py module: bcrypt hashing called directly, since passlib is incompatible with Python 3.13
c5.2: Constant-time verification, even for an account that doesn't exist
c5.3: Signed JWTs, secret key in an environment variable
c5.4: CSV import that rejects invalid rows
b1: Desktop app: search, filters and geolocation of concerts from an API.
b2: Dual-renderer survival FPS, 2D raycaster and 3D voxels, written for a game jam.
b3: Text RPG playable in the terminal: exploration, combat, crafting.
b4: Private bets between friends in virtual currency, designed for mobile.
b5: Real-time visual AI assistant, with a UI and a Windows installer.
b6: Puzzle game and Connect Four variant.
b7: Checkers game built with object-oriented programming.
t1.p: Ynov Campus Paris Ouest. Networking, advanced SQL, Python backend, security.
t2.p: Ynov. Go, Java, Git, first team projects.
t3.p: Engineering, prototyping, 3D design. Oral exam project: mount for a 360° laser level.
